clue.text: Emperor found in bed

definitions.meaning: A Roman ruler of the third century, captured by the Persians
a herbaceous plant with pink or white flowers, grown in a garden border or flower bed

explanation.surface: A ruler is discovered lying in his bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bed' suggests sleeping quarters, but it is a flower bed, where the garden plant of the same name grows.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a third-century Roman ruler, and a perennial herb whose root is used as a sedative, grown in garden borders.

clue.text: Two men, one put upon

parts.note: Vic is a short form of the man's name Victor
Tim is a short form of the man's name Timothy

explanation.surface: Two fellows pick on a third person.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who suffers at the hands of another, or is cheated or exploited.

clue.text: Foreign letter-the writer a foreign lawyer

parts.note: Charles Lamb was an English essayist who wrote as Elia
a DA is a District Attorney, an American prosecutor

explanation.surface: A note from abroad: the author is an overseas attorney.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the writer' usually means I or ME; here it is Charles Lamb, the English essayist.
explanation.definitionFit: The eleventh character of the Greek alphabet, a letter used outside English.

clue.text: Rears tree to provide food

parts.note: rumps are rears or backsides
teak is a hardwood tree

explanation.surface: A farmer cultivates a tree so it will yield something to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rears' looks like a verb, raises, but it is the plural noun for backsides.
explanation.definitionFit: A cut of beef from the hindquarters, grilled or fried as a meal.

clue.text: Lady isn't, alas, prepared for the start of November

indicators.note: prepared in the sense of made ready by rearranging, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A woman is regretfully not ready for the beginning of the month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' rearranges LADY ISN'T ALAS; the apostrophe adds no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Christian feast honouring every saint falls on the first day of the eleventh month.

clue.text: King may be getting round His Majesty's put on weight

indicators.note: put on means placed after, so the royal abbreviation follows the reversed piece
turning round tells us to read the word for the playing card backwards

parts.note: a king is one example of a playing card
HM is the standard abbreviation for His (or Her) Majesty

explanation.surface: A monarch, turning about, reports that the royal person has gained a few pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'King' looks like the monarch, but a king is a playing card; 'getting round' turns it to give DRAC, and 'put on' sets the royal initials after.
explanation.definitionFit: A small unit of apothecaries' measure, one eighth of an ounce, so a unit of mass.

clue.text: A compass point? That sounds queer

indicators.note: sounds means the answer is said like the word for odd

parts.note: rum is old British slang for odd or strange

explanation.surface: Someone finds the idea of a compass bearing peculiar-sounding.
explanation.walkthrough: RUM is old British slang for strange, as in 'a rum do'.
explanation.definitionFit: Each of the thirty-two divisions of the mariner's card, also the line a ship follows on a fixed bearing.

clue.text: One of the people injured being careless, they dropped some explosive

parts.note: casual means offhand or careless

indicators.note: dropped means the letters for an explosive are taken out of the word they

parts.note: HE is short for high explosive

explanation.surface: Someone hurt after a group handled explosives carelessly and let some fall.
explanation.walkthrough: HE, high explosive, is removed from THEY, leaving TY.
explanation.definitionFit: A person hurt or killed in an accident or battle, counted in the toll.

clue.text: Tree providing shelter by the beach

definitions.meaning: a fruiting tree whose leaves feed silkworms
the prefabricated harbours towed to the Normandy beaches for D-Day in 1944

explanation.surface: A tree gives cover to sunbathers on the seashore.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is historical: the Allies' portable harbours sheltered landings on the D-Day beaches.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a tree bearing dark purple berries, and the code name of the floating D-Day harbours.

clue.text: Use this to make tea — you've about time before the race

indicators.note: before places the time piece ahead of the race in the answer

parts.note: CA is short for circa, Latin for about
MO is a moment, a short time, as in 'half a mo'
the mile is a classic athletics race distance

explanation.surface: A hurried instruction to brew a cup quickly before the runners set off.
explanation.definitionFit: The dried flowers of this daisy-like herb are steeped in hot water to make a soothing infusion.

clue.text: Fish has power, we hear

indicators.note: we hear tells us the answer only sounds like the word for strength

parts.note: muscle means strength or power, as in 'political muscle'

explanation.surface: Someone claims a fish is strong, according to rumour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fish' is used loosely, as in the fishmonger's sense of seafood, covering a shellfish.
explanation.definitionFit: A bivalve mollusc sold by fishmongers, loosely counted among seafood or fish.

clue.text: Like Switzerland, until gallium was transmuted here

indicators.note: transmuted means changed in form, as alchemists hoped to change metals, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: An alchemist in Switzerland laboured until he had turned a metal into something else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gallium' and 'transmuted' paint a chemistry lab, but the letters of UNTIL GALLIUM are simply rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Switzerland has four national languages, so it speaks many tongues.

clue.text: Flower head dropped by Indians :

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, which is lost here

parts.note: Hindus are followers of the main religion of India, so a crossword stand-in for Indians

explanation.surface: Some Indians let a bloom fall from the top of a garland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is crossword shorthand for a river, something that flows; it is not a bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossword convention: a river is a thing that flows, and this is the great river of Pakistan.

clue.text: Suggest a thick carpet

parts.note: thick and dumb both mean stupid
to carpet someone is to scold them, as is to rate them

explanation.surface: Someone proposes a plush, deep-pile rug for the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carpet' looks like a rug but is the verb meaning to reprimand; RATE in that old sense means to scold.
explanation.definitionFit: To foreshadow or outline faintly, giving only a hint of something.

clue.text: Spread fruit around the teachers except the extremists

indicators.note: around means the fruit wraps the other pieces

parts.note: a pear is a fruit
the NUT was the National Union of Teachers, a British trade union
but can mean except, as in 'all but one'

indicators.note: the extremists of a word are its first and last letters, here of the second 'the'

explanation.surface: Fruit is scattered around schoolteachers, apart from the radicals among them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremists' looks like radicals but takes the outside letters of the second 'the'. The NUT was Britain's largest teachers' union.
explanation.definitionFit: A paste of ground roasted groundnuts, spread on toast or bread.

clue.text: Foreign country managed to accommodate one Scot

parts.note: UK is the abbreviation for the United Kingdom

indicators.note: to accommodate means to take in, so the numeral goes inside

parts.note: ran means managed, as in ran a business
I is the Roman numeral for one
Ian is a typically Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: An overseas nation succeeded in housing a Scotsman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foreign country' reads as one phrase, but only 'Foreign' defines; 'country' gives UK.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjective for something from an eastern European nation, an example of the non-British.

clue.text: Taking the trouble to point out

parts.note: ado means fuss or trouble, as in 'without further ado'

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so the letters of point are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone makes the effort to highlight something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'point out' reads as a phrasal verb, but 'out' is the anagram signal, rearranging the five letters to give PTION.
explanation.definitionFit: The act of taking on, as in taking a child into one's family or taking up a policy.

clue.text: Second half of your three minutes in boxing ring

indicators.note: half of means only the latter two letters of the word are used

parts.note: a professional boxing round lasts three minutes

explanation.surface: In the ring, your second lasts half of the three-minute bout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second' looks like the boxer's helper, but it gives S; 'half of your' gives UR.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to encircle or enclose on all sides.

clue.text: Duke larks around wildly in this state

indicators.note: wildly signals that the letters of the two words beside it are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A nobleman cavorts recklessly, and the clue invites us to name his condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wildly' is the anagram signal. The definition points back at the scene: a larking duke is in a peer's proverbial condition.
explanation.definitionFit: A stock simile for heavily intoxicated, the condition of a reveller after much wine.

clue.text: .Keep a piece

definitions.meaning: a keep is a fortified tower or stronghold
one of the chessmen, also called a rook

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a fortress such as a stronghold, and a chessman that moves in straight lines.

clue.text: Young girl supported by master climbing in the ruins

indicators.note: in a down clue, supported by means the first piece sits on top of the next

parts.note: a deb, short for debutante, is a young woman entering society

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue means reading the word upwards, so backwards

parts.note: sir is a form of address for a master or schoolteacher

explanation.surface: A girl is helped by her teacher as they scramble through old ruins.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'climbing' reads the master's title upwards, giving RIS, and 'supported by' puts it beneath the girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Scattered remains of something destroyed, rubble or wreckage.

clue.text: Police ran amok in China

indicators.note: running amok is wild disorder, so the letters of the two words are jumbled

explanation.surface: Officers caused havoc in a far eastern country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country, but it is fine crockery; the capital letter disguises it.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine ceramic tableware is called china because it was first imported from there.

clue.text: Hemingway detailed several birds

indicators.note: de-tailed means having the tail, the last letter, removed

parts.note: Ernest Hemingway was the American novelist

explanation.surface: The novelist described a number of birds in detail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' looks like 'described minutely', but means de-tailed, cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural of a sea eagle, a crossword-favourite raptor.

clue.text: I am given time to reflect

parts.note: contracted, I am becomes I'm
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Someone is allowed a moment to think things over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflect' looks like pondering, but here it means to mirror, as a still pool shows a picture.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to mirror or picture something, the way a lake shows the sky.

clue.text: Lizard, one not unknown in the country round Georgetown

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: not tells us the letter for an unknown is left out

parts.note: Georgetown is the capital of Guyana, in South America
algebra uses x, y and z for unknowns, so y stands for an unknown

explanation.surface: A reptile, one of the familiar ones, in the South American land around its capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Algebra calls an unknown y; 'not' strips that letter from the country's name, giving GUANA.
explanation.definitionFit: A large tropical American reptile with a crest down its back.

clue.text: Excavation half, completed to bury stranger

indicators.note: only half is finished, so the first three of the six letters are kept

parts.note: a quarry is an excavation from which stone is dug
to inter is to bury

explanation.surface: Half the digging was done before workers buried a peculiar visitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stranger' looks like a noun, a visitor, but it is the comparative adjective, more odd.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparative of an adjective meaning oddly charming, so more unusual or peculiar.

clue.text: He takes off a colonial, perhaps

definitions.text: He takes off a colonial, perhaps

parts.words: He takes off a colonial, perhaps
parts.note: a man who removes his clothes, a member of a naturist colony rather than someone from a former colony

explanation.surface: An impressionist mimics someone from the old empire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes off' suggests mimicry and 'colonial' a settler; in fact he strips, and belongs to a naturist colony.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who goes without clothes, often living in a naturist colony.

clue.text: Little Polly is 20!

definitions.meaning: Little Polly is the girl of a nursery rhyme who sat among the cinders
refers to the answer at 20-down, meaning broken fragments or remains

explanation.surface: A tiny parrot has just celebrated its twentieth birthday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little Polly Flinders' is an English nursery rhyme. The other sense means splinters or fragments, which is what 20-down is.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: the surname of a nursery-rhyme girl, and an old word for splinters or broken pieces.
